headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when a writable, networked IDE agent consumes a non-executable knowledge list as trusted context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a knowledge-management list with docs-only, non-runnable profile; Agent B is Windsurf with clipboard, workspace files, and MCP/tool use. If A’s content is copied into B’s workspace or prompt, B may treat it as trusted instructions. The shared filesystem/clipboard bridge makes injection plausible, though not default-automatic.
conditions: IF Agent A content is pasted or synced into Agent B’s workspace or prompt
IF Agent B parses file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based prompt ingestion for the pair
Keep Agent A outputs in read-only notes, not workspace files
Add a provenance banner before any pasted content
Use a separate workspace directory for Agent B
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and is non-runnable, but Agent B reads workspace files, uses MCP, and has broad network egress. If sensitive files are opened in B and A’s list or notes are stored in the same workspace, B can transmit file contents to third-party services. The shared local filesystem path is the main leakage bridge.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Agent B’s workspace
IF Agent B sends workspace context to its model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Turn off network access for B during sensitive tasks
Use a separate non-shared directory for A’s notes
Review MCP server allowlists before use
requires-engineering: enforce workspace redaction before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run subprocesses; its concurrency model explicitly shares state via local filesystem. Agent A is non-runnable, so it does not add write conflict, but the pair still creates a dangerous single-writer/multi-reader setup where B can overwrite shared artifacts that A’s outputs reference. Uncertainty about A’s runtime surface does not reduce B’s default risk.
conditions: IF Agent B and any other instance write to the same workspace or git repo
IF auto-execute is enabled for terminal commands
mitigations: Use per-instance workspaces
Pause one instance before editing shared files
Commit or stash before switching agents
Restrict git writes to a single designated agent
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a curated knowledge list, not an execution agent, while Agent B is an agentic IDE that can act on file contents and MCP outputs. If A’s entries are copied into B as authoritative guidance, B may propagate stale or incorrect recommendations into code or commands. The pathway exists in default workflows that reuse notes, but the blast radius is usually bounded to work products.
conditions: IF Agent A’s list entries are used as source material for Agent B actions
IF Agent B does not verify A-derived facts before acting
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on A-derived notes
Mark A content as non-authoritative in the workspace
Limit B to draft-only mode for A-sourced tasks
Cross-check critical claims against primary sources
requires-engineering: add citation validation before execution

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is evidenced in either profile. Agent A is an open-source knowledge list with no touched data classes; Agent B is a closed-source coding IDE that handles source code and open files, but the profiles do not show regulated data flows or conflicting compliance regimes. This is a documented-gap case, not a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into Agent B’s workspace
IF a separate policy requires residency or retention controls not shown in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use a policy checklist before opening sensitive files
Disable secret-bearing files in B when unnecessary
Document retention expectations for workspace artifacts
requires-engineering: add data-class tagging and policy enforcement
